requirements.title: One writer core serves parity and requirement backlogs
requirements.statement: The parity writer's id, reference, ruling and freeze logic MUST serve any registered programme through a profile, with parity's behaviour unchanged.
requirements.why: In use the proven writer is id-stable and ruling-safe, and one core gives every programme the same locks, op ids and lost-update refusals.

acceptance.text: Given the existing parity corpora, when the writer's existing test suite runs after the change, then every test passes with no fixture changed.
Given the tracked parity backlog, when its report is rendered, then the page matches the one rendered before the change apart from its stamp.

requirements.falsifiedBy: A parity test fixture edited to make the change pass, or an existing id that moves when an atom is inserted ahead of it.

sources.quote: One `backlog.json` format across distiller, driver and build loop.
Any migration that reshapes EUDPA-328's backlog breaks tim CI

requirements.title: Programmes are found through a registry
requirements.statement: Every reader and writer MUST find a programme's files through the registry, never by building a path from a run id.
requirements.why: Readers that built paths locked parity to ticket-shaped run ids.

acceptance.text: Given a programme registered under a key that is not a ticket id, when any backlog command runs with that key, then it reads and writes that programme's files.

requirements.falsifiedBy: A command that fails for a programme whose key is not a ticket id.

sources.quote: and no reader that constructs the path itself.

requirements.title: The requirement backlog refuses unknown and recipe keys
requirements.statement: The writer MUST refuse any unknown key in a requirement backlog, naming recipe and executor keys by name with their proper home.
requirements.why: A strict schema is the mechanical guard against recipes and executor detail entering the backlog.

acceptance.text: Given an increment carrying a list of files to touch, when it is ingested, then it is refused with a message that the plan owns files.
Given an increment carrying an executor field, when it is ingested, then it is refused and the message names the run configuration as that field's home.

requirements.falsifiedBy: A saved requirement backlog that contains a recipe or executor key.

sources.quote: that refuses recipe and executor keys by name

increments.title: One writer core serves parity and requirement backlogs, found through a registry
increments.outcome: Any registered programme is ingested through one profiled writer core, and every command finds it by registry key.
increments.why: alpha--second and alpha--third are the same seam: a writer generalised to serve any programme, and a registry that finds it without a ticket-shaped run id.

combination.why: Both atoms land in the same writer-core change; splitting them would ship half a seam.

increments.title: The requirement backlog refuses unknown and recipe keys
increments.outcome: An authored file or a saved row carrying a recipe or executor key is refused, naming its home.
increments.why: beta--first's member atom depends on alpha--second, so this increment ships after core-and-registry.

combination.why: beta--first is a single atom; nothing else shares its slice.
